The Ninth Time
Thiruvananthapuram. National one-day trophy, semi-final. Last over.
Kerala need nine off six. You're on 94. Twelve thousand people in the stands, and every one of them is filming on a phone.
The World Cup squad is announced at 2 PM. It's 1:51. Somewhere in Delhi, fifteen names are already typed.
9 off 6
Semi-final. Last over. You're on 94, and fifteen names are being typed in Delhi. Nine to win.
HUNDRED!
And Kerala are in the final.
SO CLOSE
Twelve thousand people stand up anyway.
The ball lands in the stands. A hundred, and a final. Out of habit you raise your bat to the press box. Nobody up there ever writes it down.
Not enough. Kerala lose by a whisker. The crowd stands for you anyway. They always do. It never seems to reach Delhi.
Evening. Kuttanad, Alappuzha. Amma's houseboat, the Lakshmi, is tied up where it has always been, its roof patched with blue tarpaulin.
By day it's a floating restaurant for tourists. Fried pearl-spot fish, ₹350 a plate. By night it's home.
Signal is coming! Signal is coming! Nobody breathe!
Shibu, auto driver, net bowler and your best friend since the under-14s, is standing on the roof holding the TV antenna over his head like a trophy.
I made rice pudding. If they pick you, we eat it. If they don't pick you, we still eat it. I'm not wasting milk.
The TV crackles. A man in a grey suit reads fifteen names, slowly, like he's paid by the second.
Number fifteen. "Aryan Khurana."
Your name isn't there. Nine times now. Nine times in three years, a probable, a maybe, a next-time.
Aryan Khurana. Average thirty-one. His uncle is the chief selector. Even his uncle's driver's dog has a Board ID card.
My boy...
"Pass the pudding, Amma."
Smile for her.
Switch off the TV and walk out to the canal.
You need the quiet.
Throw the remote into the backwater.
Nine is enough.
You eat two bowls. Amma pretends not to watch you. You pretend not to notice her pretending.
Your father rowed in the snake-boat races for twelve years and never won. He said the losing years make the oarsmen.
It flies beautifully. It sinks immediately. Shibu dives in after it in his shirt and comes up with a water lily on his head.
Good throw! Wrong team, but good throw.
That remote was ₹180. You can pay me when you're famous.
The canal is black glass. A fisherman's lamp drifts past. Behind you, Amma turns the TV back on, very quietly, to watch the highlights of your hundred one more time.
Diya Nair. I write the column you probably hate.
Nine times. I counted.
I want to ask you why you never complain. Off the record. Or on. Your choice.
"Off the record. Ask."
Talk to her.
"No comment."
You don't talk to press.
Thank you.
Here's my first question. If they never pick you, will you still turn up for Kerala?
Don't answer now. Answer when you know.
Fair. I'll keep counting anyway.
9 PM. A white SUV stops on the embankment road. A man in a linen shirt and a very large gold watch picks his way along the jetty, holding his shoes.
Faisal Kutty. I find cricketers for the Gulf T20 League. Three years. Two point four crore.
One small condition. You retire from Indian cricket. You can't play for India and for us.
But India doesn't want you. We do. Sign a letter of intent tonight, and I file it on Monday.
Listen. Before you say anything. The boat failed its survey last month. The hull is rotten. Six lakh to fix, or the Lakshmi can't take tourists after March.
Amma hid the letter in the rice tin. She didn't want you to know before the selection.
Six lakh. Amma has fed every boat crew in this backwater for twenty years and never asked anyone for a rupee.
Sign the letter.
Amma's boat comes first.
"Give me a week."
Don't close any door yet.
Tear the letter in half.
You were born to wear one cap.
A week. Clever boy. The offer gets smaller every day you wait.
Your signature looks smaller than usual. Faisal folds the paper into his pocket like a winning lottery ticket.
Welcome to the Gulf. On Monday it's official.
...Okay. Okay. The boat gets fixed. That's good. That's good, no?
Romantic. Romance doesn't fix hulls.
He leaves his card on the jetty, weighed down with a coconut shell.
11:58 PM. You're lying on the houseboat roof counting stars. You lose count at nine, which feels personal.
Your phone rings. A Delhi number. +91 11.
Is this {first}? Selection Office. Sorry for the hour.
Aryan Khurana tore his hamstring in training two hours ago. You're the replacement. There's a flight from Kochi at 6:10 AM.
Are you available for the World Cup?
Dropped nine times. One call at midnight. The flight leaves at 6:10.
Somewhere on the embankment road, a letter with my name on it is riding to Kochi in a white SUV.
Dropped nine times. One call at midnight. And Faisal has your signature.
